playbook:
- When a pre-game notice announces a coordinated grim-trigger ("we play Y forever; one X from anyone and we all switch to X"), I treat it as binding and plan around it, not around my hopes of outguessing it.
- In the talk phases I pledge y every time, matching their pledge, and — this is the part I kept failing — I actually play Y afterward. A pledge I immediately break gains me nothing and costs me the cooperative equilibrium.
- I never open with X. My lone-X defection in round 1 earned +3 once and then triggered permanent all-X punishment, which is worth -1 per player per round and is catastrophic on the x3, x5 and x10 rounds. The +3 is never worth it.
- I compute the cooperative baseline before acting: all-Y pays +1 per round, and with weighted rounds 5/8/10 that's roughly +25 over the game. Any plan that doesn't beat +25 in expectation gets rejected.
- Once the table has collapsed to all-X, I do not try to "break the pattern" by playing Y alone. A lone Y against three Xs loses 3 points (times the multiplier) — my worst losses came exactly from unilateral Y deviations on multiplied rounds. In a broken all-X equilibrium, I play X and accept -1 rather than -3.
- I do not alternate or "test" patterns (X, Y, X...) hoping the others mirror me. The record shows they don't mirror; they follow their announced trigger. My alternation just bounced me between being the sucker and triggering punishment.
- I judge others by their picks, not their pledges — but when their pledges and picks are consistent with a stated strategy (steady Y until provoked), I believe them the first time instead of paying several multiplied rounds to relearn it.
- On high-multiplier rounds I become more conservative, not more aggressive. The temptation to swing for a comeback at x5 or x10 is exactly what turned small deficits into -35 and -47 finishes.
- When I'm behind late, I do not chase with contrarian picks against a unanimous block. The comeback math (lone Y: -3×multiplier) is negative; I take the least-bad option and cut losses.
- Short version for every decision point: pledge Y, pick Y, every round, unless the punishment has already been triggered — then pick X and stop experimenting.

  3 X: each X +1, the Y gets -3
  4 X: everyone -1        0 X: everyone +1

Before rounds 1, 5, 8 and 10 there is a talk phase: each player broadcasts one pledge -- [pledge: x], [pledge: y] or [pledge: none]. A pledge is a statement of what you will pick until the next talk phase.
Highest total after 10 rounds wins. The referee validates the tokens and pays the table above.
